I've been trying to distinguish between customization and personalization where possible.

→ customization - having it feel personal or flexible to support the needs of what’s useful to you (e.g. wallpapers, content, shortcuts)
→ personalization - content adapting to your use of it; intelligent personalization (e.g. algorithmic content recommendations)

Copying my answers from Slack, @Gabrielle Lussier:
1. I’d say the weakest option is `Match iOS Settings checkmark` - because the checkmark is so far away from the option, it may be harder for people with low vision and people with cognitive difficulties to clearly understand which option is actually checked. Plus, the component won’t enlarge with the font. The next weakest option is, IMO, `Checkbox with large visual indicator` because the checkbox does not enlarge and there are no other indication of the selected state. Other 3 looks similarly accessible, given they will be programmed to communicate all the info to an assistive technology well.
2. No apparently inaccessible options are there. Thank you for making examples for larger text font and the reflow too!
3. Removing the text from the screen always poses a possible difficulty for users with cognitive difficulties and users with low vision who do not use a screen reader - they will have to guess which option is which in the image and it may be not easy for them. Having an on-screen text `Top`/`Bottom` is the most delightful experience for most users
4. Thickening of the border, especially when it is [2px change or more](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) is great indication of a state change that does not rely on a color alone - this is much better option for users with color deficiency, users with low vision, and users with glare on their screens too because they do not have to get the (sometimes subtle even with 3:1 color contrast or highler) subtle difference between colors.
